Hi Sam 1 thanks for the call and Marissa for the recap. A few technical notes ahead of our deep-dive and an example config attached. High level guidance below (we'll tune during the session):

1) Starting pool sizing (ballpark)
- Based on 5k rpm and 512-token avg with model A (quantized), expect ~0.02s per token on our target GPU for batched inference. That maps to ~10-12 tokens/ms; practical throughput per GPU depends on batching window.
- For safety start with 4 GPUs in the Dedicated pool (handles baseline with room for autoscale); configure target CPU/GPU util at 65-75% so the autoscaler has headroom.

2) Concurrency & queue sizing
- Soft concurrency per worker: 8-12 concurrent inference tasks (depends on model memory/kv cache size).
- Request queue: keep the max queue length to ~2x expected concurrency per worker with request max-age of 10s for low-latency routes. Use backpressure (503 with Retry-After) for overloaded pools.

3) Autoscaling policy (suggested)
- Scale-up triggers: queue length > 40 for 30s OR GPU util > 75% for 30s.
- Scale-down: sustained GPU util < 30% for 5m and queue length < 5.
- Cooldown: 3m between scale events to avoid flapping.

4) Embeddings & reranker guidance
- Host an embeddings endpoint on a smaller instance pool (CPU/GPU mix) for batched embedding requests; use synchronous batching and cache embeddings for recent queries.
- Reranker should run as a lightweight re-rank model (smaller transformer) with low concurrency needs but tuned for latency. Consider colocating reranker on same VPC for network locality.

5) SDK & auth notes
- For Dedicated we recommend mTLS between customer VPC and Redwood nodes + short-lived tokens issued by your identity provider. SDK supports region-based routing via route tags (we can share sample snippet).

Attached: autoscale_config_example.yaml (sample autoscaler settings, concurrency limits, and queue policy). We'll walk through this in the deep-dive and adjust with your telemetry numbers.

Regards,
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
